questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip. This strip:

options.text: Is not safe for motorcyclists at any time.
Is usually safe for motorcyclists, unless it is raining.
Should always be avoided because other parts of the lane do not have the oily strip.
Adds traction for most motorcycle tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is usually safe for motorcyclists, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: Oil drips from cars collect in a strip in the center of a traffic lane. When the road is dry, this area gives enough traction for motorcyclists to ride safely. The strip is usually only two feet wide, so you can often ride to one side of it and still be in the center part of the lane.

questions.question: Which of the following is true?

options.text: The front and rear brakes provide equal braking power.
The front brake provides more braking power than the rear brake.
The rear brake provides more braking power than the front brake.
Only the front brake should be used when braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake provides more braking power than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake on a motorcycle is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the total stopping power. Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: The center of a lane:

options.text: Is always the best part of the lane for a motorcycle.
Often contains oil and grease, but is usually safe for riding.
Often contains oil and grease, and is never safe for riding.
Is the smoothest part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often contains oil and grease, but is usually safe for riding.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip in the center of each lane. When the road is dry, this area still provides enough traction for safe motorcycle riding. Avoid riding on large buildups of oil and grease, which are common at busy intersections and toll booths.

questions.question: When going through a curve, you should:

options.text: Always stay in the same part of the lane throughout the entire curve.
Always stay in the left part of the lane throughout the entire curve.
Always stay in the right part of the lane throughout the entire curve.
Remember that the best path may not follow the curve of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remember that the best path may not follow the curve of the road.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions can change at any time. Be ready to change your lane position as needed. The best path through a curve does not always follow the curve of the road.

questions.question: When being passed from behind, you should:

options.text: Stay in the center part of the lane.
Stay in the right part of the lane.
Move onto the shoulder.
Activate your turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center part of the lane.
questions.explanation: When someone passes you from behind or from the opposite direction, stay in the center part of your lane. Moving closer to the passing vehicle puts you in danger.

questions.question: As the motorcycle's weight moves forward while braking, you:

options.text: Can apply the front brake harder.
Should use less pressure on the front brake.
Can apply the rear brake harder.
Lose traction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can apply the front brake harder.
questions.explanation: When your weight shifts forward during braking, the front wheel has more traction. This allows you to apply the front brake with more force.

questions.question: When applying the front brake, you should:

options.text: Squeeze the lever firmly and gradually increase pressure.
Grab the brake with only two fingers.
Press down on the brake lever with your foot.
Stomp on the brake lever.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the lever firmly and gradually increase pressure.
questions.explanation: To apply the front brake, use all four fingers to squeeze the brake lever firmly and smoothly. Gradually increase your pressure on the lever.

questions.question: If the throttle is stuck, you should:

options.text: Jump off the motorcycle.
Apply the brakes.
Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
Not try to twist the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
questions.explanation: If your throttle gets stuck, twist it back and forth several times to free it. If this does not work, use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch at the same time.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, which part of the lane should you usually use?

options.text: The left part of the lane
The center part of the lane
The right part of the lane
Either the left or right part of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The left part of the lane
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, ride in the left part of your lane. This keeps you away from opening car doors, people stepping out between cars, and cars pulling out of parking spaces.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should tell them to do all of the following, except:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after the engine has been started.
Sit as far forward as they can without crowding you.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.
Feel free to talk whenever they want.

questions.correctAnswerText: Feel free to talk whenever they want.
questions.explanation: Passengers should not talk or move unnecessarily so you can focus on riding. Passengers should get on the motorcycle only after the engine has started. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you and hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Debris and oil collect in the center of a traffic lane. Where is this?

options.text: The center of the lane where debris and oil from cars collect.
Where motorcycle riders should always ride for safety.
Where most accidents happen.
Where drivers are least likely to see a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center of the lane where debris and oil from cars collect.
questions.explanation: Debris and oil from cars collect in the center of a lane. Utility hole covers and other hazards are also found there.

questions.question: If your front wheel begins to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Keep using the front brake and ride out the skid.
Keep using the front brake and release the rear brake.
Release the front brake right away, then use it again.
Release the front brake and press harder on the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then use it again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks up while braking, release the front brake immediately. Then apply it again smoothly.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed.
Body weight.
How fast the alcohol was consumed.
How often a person drinks alcohol.

questions.correctAnswerText: How often a person drinks alcohol.
questions.explanation: Three main factors affect BAC: the amount of alcohol consumed, how quickly it was consumed, and body weight. A person's sex, physical condition, and food intake may also have some effect.

questions.question: Is hearing protection necessary when riding?

options.text: No, not if you wear a helmet.
Yes, in addition to wearing a helmet.
Only on windy days.
No, not if you are carrying a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, in addition to wearing a helmet.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Hearing protection helps prevent damage while still letting you hear important sounds like horns and sirens.

questions.question: If you must stop quickly while in a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Straighten up, square the handlebars, and stop.
Use both brakes hard while still leaning.
Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straighten up, square the handlebars, and stop.
questions.explanation: If you must stop quickly in a curve, straighten up and square the handlebars first, then stop. If you cannot straighten up, apply the brakes smoothly and gradually. Reduce your lean angle, then increase brake pressure as you slow down.

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip. Is this area safe for motorcyclists?

options.text: No, never safe.
Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
Usually safe, unless it is sunny.
Always safe, no matter the weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in the center of lanes. When the road is dry, this area usually has enough grip for motorcycles. The oily strip is usually less than two feet wide, so you can often ride around it and stay in the center of the lane.

questions.question: How should you swerve correctly?

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Press the handle grip in the direction you want to swerve.
Press the handle grip in the opposite direction of where you want to swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handle grip in the direction you want to swerve.
questions.explanation: To swerve and avoid a hazard, press the handle grip in the direction you want to go. To swerve left, press the left grip, then press the right to straighten. To swerve right, press the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use hard pressure on the front brake to prevent the tire from locking.
Use only the rear brake.
Use either brake, but only one at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes to slow down. Squeeze the front brake lever gradually to avoid locking the front wheel. Use gentle pressure on the rear brake.

questions.question: What is true about motorcycle windshields?

options.text: They are a good substitute for a face shield.
They are a good substitute for goggles.
They will not protect your eyes from the wind.
They protect against items thrown from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They will not protect your eyes from the wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield is not a good substitute for a face shield or goggles. Most windshields do not protect your eyes from the wind.

questions.question: If you must both brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do one action, then the other.
Do both at the same time and use extra brake pressure.
Do both at the same time, but focus mainly on swerving.
Do neither action.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: You need good traction to swerve safely, so do not brake and swerve at the same time. Instead, do one action first, then the other.

questions.question: If your front tire locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Keep pressing the brake until you stop completely.
Release both brakes and let the bike coast to a stop.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release the brake until the tire grips the road again, then brake again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the brake until the tire grips the road again, then brake again.
questions.explanation: When your front wheel locks while braking, release the brake lever until the tire grips the road again. Then apply the brake again.

questions.question: Riders wearing helmets are ________ more likely to survive a crash than those without helmets.

options.text: Two times
Three times
Eight times
Ten times

questions.correctAnswerText: Three times
questions.explanation: At any speed, wearing a helmet makes you three times more likely to survive a head injury in a crash than riding without one.

questions.question: How much stopping distance do motorcycles need in traffic?

options.text: Much less than cars.
Less than cars.
The same as cars.
More than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same as cars.
questions.explanation: In traffic, a motorcycle needs the same stopping distance as a car.

questions.question: When you are stopped, what gear should you be in?

options.text: First gear.
Neutral.
Fifth gear.
Any gear is fine.

questions.correctAnswerText: First gear.
questions.explanation: As you slow down and stop, shift down through the gears using the clutch. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if you need to.

questions.question: Which type of sign is rectangular?

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs that inform riders of road rules, like speed limits, are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.
